subject: Hosting choice & audit intake — post-call summary and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Amita Rao <amita@hexamed.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Hosting choice & audit intake — post-call summary and next steps

Hi Amita — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so your security and procurement teams have a single place to reference.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Scope: HexaMed will route both PHI-bearing requests (EHR-derived notes) and non-PHI telemetry to the inference service. Estimated PHI ratio: ~70% of requests.
- Initial traffic: ~50 rps peak (projected during triage workloads), steady-state 8–12 rps.
- Data residency: primary US region; possibility of future APAC read-only endpoints.
- Primary constraint: HIPAA/BAA and auditor access to SOC2 evidence + audit logs.

High-level hosting recommendations (based on risk and our conversation):
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool + VPC peering) as the recommended baseline for launch. Provides data isolation, predictable throughput, and admin-level network controls.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) is available if HexaMed requires customer-managed infra or air-gapped controls; this is heavier lift and requires procurement lead time.
- Hosted API could be used for non-PHI or early proof-of-concept traffic, but we should not route PHI through shared hosted endpoints without a signed BAA and agreed controls.

Immediate asks from HexaMed to qualify final path (please confirm these items):
1) Confirm whether PHI will be processed in production at launch (yes/no).
2) Provide your security questionnaire or core checklist (if you have a canonical doc).
3) Share expected go-live target (you mentioned Q4 — please confirm a target date).
4) Any procurement constraints (PO required, vendor forms) and timeline for legal review.

We attached a short one-pager that contrasts Dedicated vs Private vs Hosted and a draft BAA template for your legal to start reviewing.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- Today -> HexaMed: send security questionnaire + procurement contacts (Amita).
- 48–72 hours -> Redwood: share SOC2 summary, redacted Type II report, and pen-test high-level findings (we can gate delivery on an NDA if required).
- Week 1 -> Technical kickoff (Prio: network diagram, IP allowlist, certs, and retention/archival requirements).
- Week 2 -> If Dedicated chosen, we can spin a short POC cluster (2-week trial) and run a small sample workload to validate latency and KV cache behavior.

If this looks right I’ll draft a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with dates and owners and loop in our pricing rep for a Dedicated commitment estimate.

Best,

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
[jordan@redwood.ai]

Attachments: redwood_deploy_options_onepager.pdf (one-pager), BAA_template.docx (draft)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosting choice & audit intake — technical clarifications

Jordan / team — a few technical clarifications to surface before we finalize the recommended Dedicated config: 

1) Dedicated sizing: for ~50 rps peak with medium-length ctx (1k tokens), recommend a 4xA100-equivalent reserved pool with autoscale to 6x for bursts. That gives headroom for concurrent long-running calls and batching.
2) Latency: expected p50 ~40–80ms per token for our optimized 7B variant on that profile; p95 depends on batching policy — we can tune to meet a 300ms per-request SLO for typical prompts.
3) KV cache & Caching: for PHI-heavy workloads we suggest enabling prefix caching with strict TTLs; we can redact keys at the application layer.
4) Network: VPC peering preferred; if you need private IP only, Private deployment or our Private control plane have options for egress restrictions.

Security/evidence notes (from infra): SOC2 Type II covers our control set for production — we will provide the redacted report plus a SOC2 summary. Pen-test: quarterly internal pentests + annual third-party assessment (summary available).

I attached a short network checklist and an example cluster sizing CSV to help procurement and infra teams model costs.

— Prio

Attachments: redwood_network_requirements.csv

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Amita Rao <amita@hexamed.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting choice & audit intake — security evidence & gating checklist

Hi Amita — following up with the security evidence matrix and gating items we discussed. I’m copying the short checklist we will use to validate a Dedicated or Private deployment.

Required items for Dedicated -> production (HIPAA-ready):
- Signed BAA (we provided a draft).
- Redacted SOC2 Type II report (Control set: common criteria + system operations). Available on request; we typically share via secure link.
- Penetration test summary (third-party) — redacted findings and remediation timeline.
- Network architecture diagram showing VPC peering, customer CIDR ranges, and NAT/Egress flows.
- Audit log access & retention policy (we keep immutable audit logs for 1 year by default; retention can be extended).
- Data at-rest encryption (KMS-managed keys) and key-rotation cadence.
- Access controls: RBAC for admin console, token rotation policy, and IP allowlist support.

Optional but often requested for Private/on-prem:
- Live runbook for incident response and evidence collection steps during audits.
- Support SLA addendum for dedicated on-call for audit windows.

Delivery expectations: we can provide a secure link to the redacted SOC2 + pen-test summary within 48 business hours after we receive the security questionnaire and a signed NDA (if your legal requires). BAA review typically takes 3–5 business days from signature to finalize.

Please send over HexaMed’s security questionnaire (or point us to the doc) and the contact for your procurement/legal so we can parallelize evidence delivery and legal review.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf, BAA_template.docx, audit-log-sample.txt

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Amita Rao <amita@hexamed.ai>, procurement@hexamed.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting choice & audit intake — MAP and POC proposal

Amita / procurement team — looping back with a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a lightweight POC proposal to unblock decisioning.

Proposed MAP (owners and rough dates):
- Day 0 (today): HexaMed -> provide security questionnaire + procurement contact (owner: Amita).
- Day 1–2: Redwood -> deliver redacted SOC2 summary, pen-test summary, and BAA draft link (owner: Neha / Legal).
- Day 3–7: Legal review and BAA sign-off (owner: HexaMed legal / Redwood legal).
- Week 2: Technical kickoff to exchange network configs and sign IP allowlists (owner: HexaMed infra / Prio).
- Week 2–4: Optional Dedicated POC (2-week cluster spin-up) to validate latency, KV behavior, and integration.
- Week 4+: Decide path (Dedicated confirm or Private onboarding).

POC proposal (if you choose to proceed):
- Duration: 2 weeks
- Scope: Dedicated reserved pool sized for demo (2x A100-equivalent), sample dataset (anonymized), basic telemetry, and run three representative workloads (batch / low-latency / high-concurrency).
- Deliverables: perf report (latency/cost), integration notes, recommended config for production.
- Cost: we’ll provide a Dedicated trial price for the POC up-front (discounted) — pricing rep will follow once you confirm interest.

Next call: propose Thu, Oct 7 at 11:00 PT for legal & security to sync (30 min). Please confirm or propose an alternate slot.

If you want, I’ll also create a short one-page summary of the control evidence we’ll provide so your auditors have a single checklist to sign off.

Thanks again — we’ll stand by for the questionnaire and procurement contact.

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
[jordan@redwood.ai]
